BROCK, WILLIAM RILEY, Sheriff of Morgan County. Born in Morgan County on Sept. 8, 1873, of English-Scotch-Irish descent; his parents were Milton T. and

Cordelia T. Kesterson. His paternal grandparents were Lindsay and ( 

Brock; his maternal grandparents were

James and Elizabeth Walker Kesterson. 

Educated in the public schools of Mor gan County. Member of the Baptist 

Church; Mason; K.P.; Republican. Mr. 

Brock was elected Sheriff in August, 1936 over his opponent by an overwhelming majority. Previous to this he had served as deputy sheriff for five years. Prior to that he was in the lumber business for several years, was Postmaster at Pilot 

Mountain for twenty years, and was store manager for a lumber company. His long public career has earned for him a reputation of dependability.

His over- whelming vote on his election as sheriff is evidence of the high esteem in which he is held by the citizens of his county. 

Mr. Brock is the father of ten children:

Mrs. Delta Mae Smith; Virgil Brock; 

Mrs. Mabel Emerson; Otto Brock; Mrs. 

Bertie Anderson; Ava Brock; Carl T. 

Brock; Edward Brock; Hazel; William 

Riley, Jr. Mr. Brock has eleven grandchildren. He says that his hobby is "making friends.'' His grandfather 

Kesterson and his father fought with the

Federal forces during the Civil War. 

He was first married to Malissa M. 

Phipps on August 2, 1892, and later to 

Susie Gann on January 15, 1900.

DAGLEY, GEORGE WASHINGTON, County Judge and Lawyer. Mr. Dagley was elected County Judge in 1934. Prior to that he was engaged in the practice of law at Wartburg. He served as

Trustee of Morgan County from 1924 to 

1930. Before being elected to public office he served the public by teaching in the public schools of Morgan County for a period of twelve years. 

His long record of service before the public has especially fitted him for the office he now holds. The high esteem in which he is held throughout the county is evidence of his efficiency in the conducting of the affairs of his office. During the World 

War he served in Company A, 307 Military Police. He enlisted October 4, 1917, went to Camp Gordon, near Atlanta,

Georgia, and thence to France by way of 

England at Le Havre, France. After spending about 7 months in France he returned to the United States and was discharged from Camp Gordon on Feb. 

19, 1919. He was wounded in the leg on the Verdun Front on September 28, 1918, while piloting ambulances, supplies and ammunition trains. He was Repub lican Election Commissioner of Morgan 

County for two terms, beginning in 1930.

He has also served as Chairman of the 

Republican Executive Committee for about six years. He was married to Reba 

Chester, Dec. 24, 1920. He is the father of four children: Russell L. Dagley, 16; 

Lee Chester Dagley, 13; George W., Jr., 11; Myra Gene Dagley, 9. His hobby is fox hunting.

As at- torney at law, farmer, coal operator in

Brumett. Educated in the public schools of Morgan County, Cumberland University, LL.B. in 1918. Mr. Justice was elected to the lower House in 1907, and 1935, and was elected to the State Senate in 1937-the 70th General Assembly.

Regina Jones before their marriage on

SCHUBERT, CARL F., Merchant and 

Justice of the Peace. Mr. Schubert has been in the mercantile business practically all his life and for himself for twenty years. Mr. Schubert was elected 

Justice of the Peace for the 4th District of Morgan County in August, 1936, in which election he led the ticket by a substantial majority in a field of eight. 

Mr. Schubert, during his long service before the public, has acquired a reputation of dependability, and his circle of friends embraces the entire county. He enlisted for service in the World War on Sept. 

19, 1917, serving first in Company D., 307 Engineers, and later in Company A., 113 Machine Gun Battalion. He was promoted from Private to Corporal on 

March 1, 1918, and to Sergeant on July 

18, 1918. He was overseas from May 19, 1918 to Apr. 2, 1919, and was discharged 

Apr. 12, 1919. He served one year as commander of Morgan County American 

Legion Post, and six years as Post Adjt. 

He was born at Wartburg, Tennessee on 

August 16, 1895 of German-Swiss descent.

His parents were Bruno and Louisa Zumstein Schubert; paternal grandparents were Frank and Minnie Baudt Schubert; maternal grandparents were John and 

Caroline Gerber Zumstein. Educated in the public schools of Morgan County,

Knoxville Business College, Knoxville, 

Tennessee. Member of St. Paul's Lutheran Church; Democrat. He married 

Miss Ina Rogers on July 2, 1927; he is a hobbyist, and his hobby is the culture of flowers.

William Asbury Stringfield and Lydia D. 

Freels Stringfield on April 7, 1887 in

Morgan County, Tennessee. Paternal grandparents were James and Lowe

WOLF RIVER YORK, SGT. ALVIN C., Farmer, stock raiser, and promoter of educational institutions. Born in Fentress County, Tennessee on December 13, 1887, of 

Dutch-English descent, to William and 

Mary Brooks York; his father was a farmer and blacksmith. Paternal grandparents were Uriah York and Eliza Livingston York; maternal grandparents were William and Nancy Riles Brooks. 

Attended the public schools of Fentress 

County. Member of the Church of Christ; 

Democrat; American Legion. Alvin C.

York was born in a one-room log cabin among the mountains in Fentress County in the most modest circumstances. He began life along the banks of Wolf River, known to those of his section as the last of the Long Hunters, a trait which followed his ancestry and found its way in his life and in the same section where for three generations before him the crack of the musket was the order of the day in the lives of these stalwart mountain folk; his great-grandfather

Cunrad Piles planted the first settlement from which after more than a century and a half was to come the man of destiny, the most renowned military hero of the World War. Though conscientiously opposed to war and his religious belief forbidding his services as a soldier, after many weary hours spent under the open sky of the mountain side in holy communion with his Maker, his decision was that which resulted in his becoming the leading character in all the American 

Expeditionary Forces in Europe, and of all the Allied Armies-which assertion is warranted by the words of Marshall 

Foch, who said of him, "What you did was the greatest thing accomplished by "" He any private soldier of the war. single-handed captured 132 Germans, three of whom were officers, took about 

35 machine guns, and killed no less than 

25 of the enemy. His military training, except for that received in everyday life, was of short duration; he was admitted on Nov. 15, 1917 and later as Sgt. was assigned to Company G., 328th Infantry, 82nd Division. During the time of his services in the army he came to realize more than ever before the need of an education of which he had been deprived, having reached only the second grade. 

He, therefore, upon his return to the states, promised himself that the children of his section of the state should be given better advantages for an education than he had had-thus he began the promotion of educational institutions. York

PROMINENT TENNESSEANS 

285 was thirty-one years old at the time of his heroic capture of the enemy. When he was drafted into service, he was sent to Camp Gordon for training on November 15, 1917. He did not believe in war.

It was against his religion and in his war record in the War Department in 

Washington, D.C., there is a little narrow pink slip marked "Conscientious Objector, York, Alvin C." However, he was not released and went on to become the most talked-of man of the World 

War. He was married to Miss Gracie 

Williams on June 7, 1919; he is the father of six children: Alvin Cullum, Jr., aged 

16; George Edward, aged 13; Woodrow 

Wilson, aged 11; Andrew Jackson, aged 

7; Betsie Ross, aged 4; and Mary Alice, aged 2. In the mountains of his home he was known as being very religious, and was called the "singing elder." He is really worthy of the appellation, "hero."

County, Tennessee. Born in Cannon 

County, Tennessee, of Scotch-Irish ancestry, on March 12, 1885 to James B. and Climmie Finley Smith. Paternal grandparents were Robert A. and Myra 

George Smith; maternal grandparents were Joseph and Zenobia Foster Finley. 

Mr. Smith was elected Sheriff of Cannon

County in August, 1934, and re-elected in August, 1936, being elected by an overwhelming majority at his last election. Prior to his election as sheriff he was for seventeen years a member of the

County Court. Mr. Smith has been engaged in farming and livestock raising and for many years was engaged in the mercantile business. He was married to

Lizzie Mai Smith on December 13, 1908. 

He is the father of five children: Mary 

George, Mrs. Scyrene Hayes, Glaydas 

Pearl, Kenneth Zenobia, and Grace; he is the grandfather of three grandchildren; Newburn, Norman, and Ronald

Hayes. He was educated in the public schools of Cannon County. He is a member of the Christian Church; a Democrat.
